chunks: Among them, the virtue of the Qur'an:

The Qur'an orders and refrains, is silent yet speaks. It is Allah's proof upon His creation. He took a pledge from them upon it, and mortgaged their souls to it. He perfected its light, and honored his religion through it. He gathered His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while He had finished conveying to the creation all the rulings of guidance through it. So magnify Him, may He be glorified, as He magnified Himself, for He has not concealed from you anything of His religion, nor left out anything He approved or disapproved, except that He made for it a clear sign and a decisive verse, which repels you from it or calls you to it. His pleasure in what remains is one, and His wrath in what remains is one.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and theological virtues of the Quran according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this passage underscores the concept of *Kamal al-Din* (perfection of religion), affirming that the Qur'an contains all necessary rulings for guidance, leaving no ambiguity for the faithful. It highlights the Qur'an as the enduring *Hujjah* (proof) of Allah, establishing a direct covenant where the text itself serves as the visible sign (*alam*) for every divine command or prohibition. This reinforces the Shia belief in the sufficiency of the Qur'an for legal and spiritual matters, complementing the role of the Ahl al-Bayt in its interpretation.
